newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends lower on crackdown jitters.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends lower on crackdown jitters.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Wednesday as foreign investors sold on expectations Beijing would announce new measures to crack down on speculation, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index fell 0.53 points or 0.33 percent to close at 158.81 on turnover of HK$74.7 million, compared with Tuesday's HK$91.4 million.

The domestic currency A share market rose 4.27 points or 0.91 percent to 474.17 on an extended rebound that began on Monday, after recent government anti-speculation measures caused sharp losses, brokers said.
Turnover on the A share market was 8.0 billion yuan against 9.7 billion yuan the previous session.

"Foreign investors were seen selling, especially some recently-listed B shares, because they are afraid Beijing will soon announce new crackdown measures," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.

Brokers said the B share market remained overshadowed by a front-page report in Hong Kong's South China Morning Post on Tuesday saying China's central government has plans to further depress share prices.
The newspaper reported that China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong had vowed to take further action to stop speculation and punish officials guilty of improper conduct.

But the A share market did not lose ground on Tuesday and Wednesday because domestic investors were betting any new clampdown policy would not be severe with the handover of Hong Kong less than a month away, brokers said.
The British colony of Hong Kong is to revert to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30.
"But the markets are vulnerable to negative news and investors are becoming increasingly sensitive," an analyst with a Western investment bank in Shenzhen said.
Brokers said they expected cautious trading ahead, with the 160-point level seen as the short-term resistance for the B share index.

On the B share market, newcomer Nanjing Posts and Telecommunication slipped HK$0.07 to HK$4.18 on volume of 3.81 million shares due to selling by foreign institutions, brokers said. It was the most actively traded B share issue.

Buying targeted B shares of Shenzhen-based companies as some investors expected Hong Kong's reversion to China to boost neighbouring Shenzhen as economic ties between the two cities develop, brokers said.
Shenzhen-based Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd was the best performer and rose HK$0.42 or 8.47 percent to HK$5.38.
On the A share market, the sharpest gainer was Xibei Bearing Co, which surged 10 percent to its limit-up at 11.40 yuan.
